cases.sentence: ___ показался ему знаменательным и занимательным, и очень, очень понравился.
options: разговор
разговора
разговору
разговором
cases.translation: The conversation seemed significant and interesting to him, and he liked it very, very much.
cases.explain: "Разговор" is the subject of the verb "показался" (seemed), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: А Засимову велю ночевать у ___, чтоб он был под рукой.
options: хозяйка
хозяйки
хозяйке
хозяйкой
cases.translation: And I'll order Zossimov to spend the night at the landlady's, so he'll be close at hand.
cases.explain: The preposition "у" (at/by) always governs the genitive case, giving "хозяйки."

cases.sentence: Я давеча Лужину сказал, что его с лестницы спущу и прогнал его к ___.
options: чёрт
чёрта
чёрту
чёртом
cases.translation: I told Luzhin earlier that I'd throw him down the stairs, and I chased him to the devil.
cases.explain: The preposition "к" (toward) always governs the dative case, giving "чёрту."

cases.sentence: «Пойдемте, маменька, хоть из комнаты выйдем на ___!» — шепнула испуганная Дуня.
options: минута
минуты
минуте
минуту
cases.translation: "Let's go, mama, let's at least step out of the room for a minute!" whispered the frightened Dunya.
cases.explain: The preposition "на" expressing a span of time governs the accusative case here, giving "минуту."

cases.sentence: Дуня, — с ___ продолжал Раскольников, — я этого брака не желаю.
options: усилие
усилия
усилию
усилием
cases.translation: "Dunya," Raskolnikov continued with an effort, "I do not want this marriage."
cases.explain: The preposition "с" describing manner ("with effort") governs the instrumental case, giving "усилием."

cases.sentence: Авдотья Романовна была бледна, рука ее дрожала в ___ брата.
options: рука
руки
руке
рукой
cases.translation: Avdotya Romanovna was pale; her hand trembled in her brother's hand.
cases.explain: The preposition "в" marking location governs the prepositional case, giving "руке."

reading.ru: Раскольников приподнялся и сел на диване.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov do as this section opens?
options: He sits up on the sofa
He jumps out of bed and runs outside
He falls back asleep immediately
He begins shouting angrily at his mother
reading.correct: He sits up on the sofa
reading.explain: The section opens with Raskolnikov raising himself up and sitting down on the sofa.

reading.ru: «Да что вы думаете!» — кричал Разумихин, еще более возвышая голос.
reading.question: What is Razumikhin doing in this scene?
options: Shouting loudly, raising his voice even more, while defending the mother and sister
Quietly reading a letter
Sleeping soundly on the sofa
Arguing with Porfiry Petrovich about the murder
reading.correct: Shouting loudly, raising his voice even more, while defending the mother and sister
reading.explain: Razumikhin shouts, raising his voice even higher, as he defends the mother and sister from Pulkheria Alexandrovna's timid interruption.

reading.ru: «Слушай, — сказал он Засимову, — ты малый и славный, но ты, кроме всех твоих скверных качеств, еще и потаскун.
reading.question: What does Razumikhin say about Zossimov as they near Raskolnikov's apartment?
options: That despite his good qualities, he is also a womanizer
That he is a brilliant doctor with no faults
That he is too shy around women
That he never speaks to Raskolnikov
reading.correct: That despite his good qualities, he is also a womanizer
reading.explain: Razumikhin tells Zossimov he's a decent fellow but, among his bad qualities, is also a womanizer.

reading.ru: «Кстати, имеешь ты какое-нибудь влияние на тех-то, на мать да сестру?
reading.question: What does the speaker ask about, right before advising caution with Raskolnikov?
options: Whether he has any influence over the mother and sister
Whether the mother and sister have already left for home
Whether the mother and sister know about the murder
Whether the mother and sister have any money left
reading.correct: Whether he has any influence over the mother and sister
reading.explain: He asks whether the listener has any influence over the mother and sister, adding that they should be more careful with Raskolnikov that day.

reading.ru: Господи, одиннадцатый час».
reading.question: What does Razumikhin silently observe about Pulkheria Alexandrovna's gold watch, glimpsed as she checks the time?
options: That it must be a gift from her daughter's fiancé
That it is broken and shows the wrong time
That it was stolen from a shop
That it belonged to Raskolnikov's late father
reading.correct: That it must be a gift from her daughter's fiancé
reading.explain: As Pulkheria Alexandrovna checks her elegant gold watch, which clashes with the rest of her modest clothing, Razumikhin privately thinks, "A gift from the fiancé."

reading.ru: Умрите, собаки, если вы несчастливы.
reading.question: What sarcastic principle does Raskolnikov mock in this outburst about needing 'the right' to help someone?
options: That people supposedly must first earn 'the right' to help others, or else 'die, you dogs, if you are unhappy'
That government aid is always French in origin
That money is worthless in modern society
That helping others is impossible without royal permission
reading.correct: That people supposedly must first earn 'the right' to help others, or else 'die, you dogs, if you are unhappy'
reading.explain: Raskolnikov bitterly mocks the idea that one must first have 'the right' to help someone, sarcastically adding 'Die, you dogs, if you are unhappy,' and calling it a 'French' notion before laughing and asking Dunya if that isn't so.

reading.ru: А чего ты опять краснеешь?
reading.question: What does the speaker accuse his sister of, right after asking why she is blushing again?
options: Lying
Stealing
Cheating on her fiancé
Hiding money
reading.correct: Lying
reading.explain: Right after asking why she is blushing again, he tells her, 'You're lying, sister.'

reading.ru: Мы давеча с Катериной Ивановной все рассчитали, так что и останется, чтобы помянуть.
reading.question: What practical matter has the speaker calculated together with Katerina Ivanovna?
options: How to arrange the funeral cheaply enough to still afford a memorial meal
How to pay off Marmeladov's old debts
How to buy a new apartment
How to send money to Raskolnikov's mother
reading.correct: How to arrange the funeral cheaply enough to still afford a memorial meal
reading.explain: The speaker explains that he and Katerina Ivanovna have calculated everything so there will be enough left over for a memorial meal after the funeral.

reading.ru: Думал он, припоминая лицо Сони.
reading.question: Whose face is Raskolnikov trying to place, feeling he has seen it somewhere before?
options: Sonya's face
Porfiry Petrovich's face
Zamyotov's face
Svidrigailov's face
reading.correct: Sonya's face
reading.explain: He thinks this while trying to recall Sonya's face, feeling he has seen it somewhere before and that he needs to find out where.

reading.ru: Тревожно подумал Раскольников.
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov feel in this tense exchange, right before Zamyotov's reaction is described?
options: Anxious
Completely calm and relaxed
Amused and lighthearted
Bored and indifferent
reading.correct: Anxious
reading.explain: The narrator notes that Raskolnikov thought this anxiously, just before Zamyotov appears somewhat, though not greatly, embarrassed.

reading.ru: Про приезд матери не знал.
reading.question: What detail does the text say a certain person did NOT know about?
options: That Raskolnikov's mother had arrived in town
That Raskolnikov had pawned his watch
That Raskolnikov had a fever
That Raskolnikov had left the city
reading.correct: That Raskolnikov's mother had arrived in town
reading.explain: The passage notes he knew about the previous evening but did not know about the mother's arrival.

reading.ru: С каким-то даже испугом осведомился Разумихин.
reading.question: With what emotion does Razumikhin ask his question in this exchange with Porfiry Petrovich?
options: With a kind of fright/alarm
With great amusement
With total indifference
With open hostility
reading.correct: With a kind of fright/alarm
reading.explain: The text says Razumikhin inquired with something like fright, to which Porfiry replies that it wasn't entirely for that reason.

reading.ru: Это и наказание ему опричь каторги.
reading.question: What theory are Porfiry and Razumikhin discussing in this exchange?
options: Whether truly great, exceptional people are exempt from suffering for their crimes
Whether the weather affects criminal behavior
Whether women should be allowed to study law
Whether Sonya should be arrested
reading.correct: Whether truly great, exceptional people are exempt from suffering for their crimes
reading.explain: They discuss whether awareness of one's guilt is itself a punishment beyond hard labor, and whether the truly 'great' or 'genius' criminals are exempt from such suffering, referencing Raskolnikov's article on extraordinary men.

reading.ru: Не найдя ничего, он встал и глубоко перевел дыхание.
reading.question: What is Raskolnikov doing when he searches a hole in the wallpaper and finds nothing?
options: Looking for evidence or stolen items he fears he may have left behind
Looking for a letter from his mother
Looking for money he had saved
Looking for a weapon to use against Porfiry
reading.correct: Looking for evidence or stolen items he fears he may have left behind
reading.explain: Raskolnikov anxiously searches a hole in the wallpaper where stolen items had once been hidden, finds nothing, and stands up, breathing deeply in relief.

reading.ru: Это та самая квартира, в которой работники мазали.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov realize about the apartment where workers are now painting?
options: That it is the very apartment (the murder scene) he was looking for
That it belongs to his mother
That it is Sonya's apartment
That it is Porfiry's office
reading.correct: That it is the very apartment (the murder scene) he was looking for
reading.explain: He recognizes that this is the very apartment where the workmen are painting — the scene of the murder — surprised he did not recognize it at once.

reading.ru: Как спрашивали, так и отвечал.
reading.question: How does the speaker describe responding to questions put to him?
options: He simply answered exactly as he was asked, with an air of simplicity
He refused to answer any questions
He lied about everything he was asked
He answered only in writing
reading.correct: He simply answered exactly as he was asked, with an air of simplicity
reading.explain: He says he answered just as he was asked, adding this with a surprising expression of simple-heartedness.

reading.ru: Только что его похоронили, и я крикнул, забывшись, — Фелька, трубку!
reading.question: What odd anecdote does the speaker tell about his deceased servant Filka?
options: That right after Filka's funeral, he absentmindedly called out for him to bring his pipe
That Filka came back as a ghost
That Filka stole his pipe before dying
That Filka's death was never explained
reading.correct: That right after Filka's funeral, he absentmindedly called out for him to bring his pipe
reading.explain: The speaker recounts that just after Filka's funeral he forgot himself and shouted, 'Filka, my pipe!' before going to the cabinet where his pipes stand.

reading.ru: Он очень странный и на что-то решился.
reading.question: What do the characters suspect about the strange man who arrived right after his wife's funeral?
options: That he seems to have resolved on some secret plan and knows something
That he is planning to remarry immediately
That he is a police informant
That he intends to leave the country at once
reading.correct: That he seems to have resolved on some secret plan and knows something
reading.explain: The characters remark that this man, who arrived right after his wife's funeral, is very strange and seems to have made up his mind about something, as if he knows something.

reading.ru: Раскольников замолчал и обратился к своему чаю.
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov do instead of answering what Luzhin wants to propose to Dunya?
options: He falls silent and turns his attention to his tea
He immediately explains everything in detail
He storms out of the room
He starts laughing loudly
reading.correct: He falls silent and turns his attention to his tea
reading.explain: Rather than answering the frightened Pulkheria Alexandrovna's question about what Luzhin wants to propose, Raskolnikov falls silent and turns to his tea.

reading.ru: Явилась девушка гордая.
reading.question: How does Luzhin imagine Dunya in his private fantasies about their marriage?
options: As a proud girl of superior upbringing who will be endlessly grateful to him
As someone beneath him in every way
As a wealthy heiress who needs nothing from him
As someone who will control their marriage completely
reading.correct: As a proud girl of superior upbringing who will be endlessly grateful to him
reading.explain: Luzhin pictures a proud, virtuous girl, superior to him in upbringing and refinement, who will nonetheless be slavishly and eternally grateful to him for his 'heroic' act of marrying her.

reading.ru: «Так, мне очень надо», — ответил он смутно, как бы колеблясь в том, что хотел сказать Дуне.
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov answer Dunya when she asks where he is going?
options: Vaguely, saying only that he really needs to, as if hesitating over what to tell her
He tells her the complete truth immediately
He refuses to answer and walks away silently
He asks her to come along with him
reading.correct: Vaguely, saying only that he really needs to, as if hesitating over what to tell her
reading.explain: He answers vaguely, 'Just because I really need to,' seeming to hesitate over what he actually wanted to say to Dunya, though his pale face shows sharp resolve.

reading.ru: Она так верит, что во всем справедливость должна быть.
reading.question: What does the speaker say about this woman's (Sonya's) belief in justice?
options: That she firmly believes justice must exist in everything, and demands it
That she has given up believing in justice
That she believes only in luck
That she cares nothing for fairness
reading.correct: That she firmly believes justice must exist in everything, and demands it
reading.explain: The speaker says she so firmly believes there must be justice in everything that she even demands it.

reading.ru: Бог Повторяла она, не помня себя.
reading.question: What does Sonya keep repeating, overwhelmed with emotion, in this scene?
options: "God", oblivious to herself
Raskolnikov's name
Her father's name
A prayer for money
reading.correct: "God", oblivious to herself
reading.explain: Beside herself, Sonya keeps repeating the word "God," right after saying God will protect her, and just before Raskolnikov's skeptical retort that perhaps there is no God at all.

reading.ru: И многие из иудеев пришли к Марфе и Марии утешать их в печали о братьях.
reading.question: What is Sonya doing in this scene, reading aloud up to the nineteenth verse?
options: Reading aloud the Gospel story of the raising of Lazarus
Reading a letter from Raskolnikov's mother
Reading a newspaper report about the murder
Reading a poem she wrote herself
reading.correct: Reading aloud the Gospel story of the raising of Lazarus
reading.explain: Sonya reads aloud from the Gospel of John, the account of Lazarus, including how many Jews came to comfort Martha and Mary over their brother's death.

reading.ru: До того понравился, что он и стул перенес, чтоб на будущее время, хоть завтра, например, не подвергаться опять неприятности простоять целый час на ногах, а устроиться покомфортнее, чтоб уж во всех отношениях получить удовольствие.
reading.question: Why does the eavesdropper move a chair closer, according to this passage?
options: So he won't have to stand for a whole hour next time he listens in, and can sit comfortably
So he can offer it to a guest
So he can reach a high shelf
So he can block the door
reading.correct: So he won't have to stand for a whole hour next time he listens in, and can sit comfortably
reading.explain: The passage reveals that the listener enjoyed the overheard conversation so much that he moved a chair over, so that next time he would not have to stand for a whole hour and could listen in greater comfort.
